text:
The "interrogation" by security you get when leaving at Ben Gurion airport (or before boarding a flight to Israel, if flying El Al or another Israeli airline) is completely separate from border control. So don't stress about what happened there :) 

Make sure your partner has an ETA-IL - that will be necessary for him to board his flight. It's definitely not illegal for a foreigner to visit Israel with their Israeli partner, but border control is there to make sure that someone isn't coming into Israel as a "tourist" when their real intention is to settle and live here. Red flags include many recent trips to Israel, or recent extended visits, limited connections to the country you are living, no return flight, and having no real plans to tell them about what you are wanting to do on your visit. 

So make sure you have a return ticket (ideally one that isn't months in the future), have a short and sharp answer ready about what you are planning to do and where you will stay (visiting family etc. is fine), and if you want to be really sure your husband could bring documents showing his connection to the country he is living - e.g. a rent contract, a letter from his employer stating that he is working there and on leave etc. 

But honestly, unless he has been on long or very frequent visits to Israel recently, as an American I would think he is likely to be okay.
